column1: # ACTION SE, the OFFLINE half: group every live slug by its repo half and look for repeated
# names under different owners. 8 live shelves, archive/ excluded.
# DEFECT FOUND IN THIS INSTRUMENT BEFORE PUBLISHING (T225-1):
#   the first run reported 118 "pairs". GitHub OWNER names are case-INSENSITIVE, so OpenOLAT
#   and openolat are ONE account spelled two ways, not two owners. 28 of the 118 were owner-case
#   variants only. The unit is the ACCOUNT, not the spelling.
# SECOND DEFECT (T225-2), the API-path phantom owner:
#   api.github.com/repos/OWNER/REPO matches a bare "github.com/" and yields owner "repos".
#   Sibling of p224's T224-2 dotted-owner rule: the guard must reject the API path too.
# GUARDS APPLIED: owner = alnum+hyphen only (T224-2); owner casefolded (T225-1).
# distinct repo names on the live shelves:
# of those, confirmed ALIAS pairs by the ref-set oracle:
# NAME-SHARING IS NOT ALIASING. 19 independent projects are called canvas-mcp and 10 are
# called moodle-mcp; those are a crowded namespace, not duplicate carrying. Only the
# ref-set oracle separates the two, which is why SE's limb 1 rests on 4 pairs, not 90.
# THE KB's OWN CITATION DEFECT - accounts spelled 2+ ways across the shelves.
# Harmless to a reader, NOT harmless to any grep-keyed census: each spelling becomes its
# own bucket, which is how a 118 appeared where the answer was 90.
# CANDIDATES: repo names under 2+ distinct accounts, ranked by mentions.
# Unprobed rows are NOT claims of aliasing - they are the queue the oracle runs on.
